name: Parallel Structure
summary: Keeping lists and comparisons grammatically balanced.

paragraphs: When you list several items or compare two things, English expects them to have the same grammatical shape. Reading, writing and speaking is balanced: three -ing forms. Reading, writing and to speak is not, because the last item suddenly changes shape.

This idea is called parallel structure. It rarely changes the meaning, but it makes a big difference to how polished your writing sounds. Unbalanced lists feel clumsy, while balanced ones read smoothly and look carefully planned. The rule is simple: match the forms on both sides of and, or, but, than and pairs like not only… but also.

blocks.title: The rule in one line
blocks.text: Items joined by and, or, than or both… and must have the same form: noun + noun, -ing + -ing, to + to.

paragraphs: Parallel structure is a sign of controlled, mature writing. Examiners notice when lists and comparisons are well balanced, and they also notice when they are not, especially in introductions and conclusions, where you often list your main points.
Task 2 essays use lists constantly: reasons, causes, solutions and examples. Making each list parallel is a quick way to make your sentences more accurate and more sophisticated.

sections.title: Rule 1: Every item in a list has the same form
sections.label: Rule 1: Every item in a list has the same form

paragraphs: When you list three or more items, each one should have the same grammatical form. If the first item is a noun, they should all be nouns. If the first is an -ing form, they should all be -ing forms.
The error usually appears in the last item, because by then the writer has forgotten how the list started.

rows: Nouns
Cities offer jobs, education and entertainment.
-ing forms
Reading, writing and speaking are all important.
to + verb
The aim is to reduce costs, save time and protect jobs.
Adjectives
The course was cheap, flexible and useful.

items.text: Students need time, money and to be motivated.
Students need time, money and motivation.

sections.title: Rule 2: Pairs joined by and, or and but
sections.label: Rule 2: Pairs joined by and, or and but

paragraphs: The same rule applies to two items joined by and, or or but. Both halves should match. A quick check: read each half separately with the start of the sentence and see if both sound correct.
Pay particular attention to verbs. If one verb is in the past simple, the other one usually should be too.

items.text: Many people prefer cycling or to walk to work.
Many people prefer cycling or walking to work.
He studied hard and passes the exam.
He studied hard and passed the exam.

sections.title: Rule 3: Comparisons with than and as
sections.label: Rule 3: Comparisons with than and as

paragraphs: When you compare two things, both sides of than or as should have the same form. Compare an activity with an activity, and a noun with a noun.
This is very common in Task 2: It is better to prevent crime than to punish it, or Walking is healthier than driving.

items.text: Living in a city is more exciting than to live in the countryside.
Living in a city is more exciting than living in the countryside.
It is cheaper to cook at home than eating out.
It is cheaper to cook at home than to eat out.

paragraphs: In comparisons, make sure you are comparing the same kind of thing. The population of Tokyo is larger than London compares a population with a city, which is not logical.
Use that of (singular) or those of (plural) to repeat the first noun: The population of Tokyo is larger than that of London. This is especially useful in Task 1.

items.text: Prices in City A were higher than City B.
Prices in City A were higher than those in City B.
The salary of a doctor is higher than a teacher.
The salary of a doctor is higher than that of a teacher.

paragraphs: Some linking words come in pairs. Whatever comes after the first word should have the same form as what comes after the second word.
Not only… but also is a popular choice in Task 2, so it is worth getting right. If not only is followed by a verb, but also should be followed by a verb too.

rows: both… and
Both parents and teachers play a role.
either… or
Students can either study online or attend classes.
neither… nor
The plan is neither cheap nor practical.
not only… but also
Exercise not only improves health but also reduces stress.

items.text: Exercise is not only good for the body but also improves mood.
Exercise not only benefits the body but also improves mood.

paragraphs: In a list, you can repeat a small word (to, the, by) before every item, or use it only once at the start. Both are correct. Problems arise when you repeat it for some items but not for others.
Choose one pattern and keep it.

items.text: to save time, money and energy
to save time, to save money and to save energy
to save time, money and to save energy

paragraphs: Task 1 reports often describe two or three trends in one sentence. Keeping the verbs in the same tense and form helps the reader compare the trends at a glance.
When you describe several changes, use the same pattern for each: verb + adverb, or a + adjective + noun.

rows: Coffee sales rose sharply, while there was a slight fall in tea.
Coffee sales rose sharply, while tea sales fell slightly.
The number of cars doubled and a large increase in bikes.
The number of cars doubled, and the number of bikes rose sharply.

sections.title: Rule 8: Check your introduction and conclusion
sections.label: Rule 8: Check your introduction and conclusion

paragraphs: Your introduction often previews the main points, and your conclusion often summarizes them. These are exactly the places where long, unbalanced lists appear.
Before you finish, read your thesis statement and conclusion slowly and check every list. A balanced thesis makes a strong first impression.

items.text: This essay will discuss the causes of obesity, its effects and how to solve it.
This essay will discuss the causes and effects of obesity, as well as possible solutions.
Governments should invest in education, improving healthcare and to create jobs.
Governments should invest in education, improve healthcare and create jobs.

paragraphs: Here is how parallel structure looks in real IELTS writing.

rows: Task 1
Coal use fell, gas use rose and nuclear use remained stable.
three past simple verbs
Task 1
Prices in City A were higher than those in City B.
like with like
Task 2
Cities offer better jobs, schools and hospitals.
three nouns
Task 2
It is better to prevent crime than to punish it.
to + to
Task 2
Exercise not only improves health but also reduces stress.
verb + verb

paragraphs: These five errors are among the most common parallel structure mistakes in IELTS essays.

rows: reading, writing and to speak
reading, writing and speaking
better than to live in a village
better than living in a village
higher than City B
higher than that in City B
not only cheap but also saves time
not only cheap but also quick
time, money and to be motivated
time, money and motivation

paragraphs: Use this routine on every list and comparison.

steps: Find every list and every pair joined by and, or, but or than.
Look at the first item and note its form: noun, -ing, to + verb or adjective.
Make every other item match that form.

furtherStudy.title: Purdue OWL: Parallel Structure
furtherStudy.description: Rules and examples for balanced lists and comparisons.

cards.why: The list starts with -ing forms, so every item should be an -ing form.

cards.front: The job requires patience, skill and ____.
cards.why: The list is made of nouns, so the last item should be a noun too.

cards.front: It is better to prevent crime than ____ it.
cards.why: The first side uses to + verb, so the second side should match.

cards.front: Prices in Dhaka are higher than ____ in Sylhet.
cards.why: We are comparing prices (plural), so we use those to repeat the noun.

cards.front: The population of Tokyo is larger than ____ of London.
cards.why: We are comparing populations, and population is singular, so we use that.

cards.front: Students can either study online ____ attend classes on campus.
Exercise not only improves health ____ reduces stress.
cards.why: Not only always pairs with but also.

cards.front: She studied hard and ____ the exam.
cards.why: Both verbs describe the past, so both should be in the past simple.
The first side uses an -ing form (walking), so the second side should match.

cards.front: The city is clean, safe and ____.
cards.why: The list is made of adjectives, so the last item should be an adjective too.
